title: Regional Safeweight Controller and LTS Rollforward for Hosted API
creator: Maya Singh
description: Background: We need to harden hosted API deployments for multi-region rollouts while preserving LTS channel guarantees. In prior rollouts we observed short-lived traffic surges and cache-warmup-related latencies that breached SLOs during weighted traffic shifts. Objective: implement a 'Safeweight Controller' — an automated controller that stages weight changes per-region with adaptive hold windows based on real-time SLO signals, token-level error rate, and KV cache warm metrics. Coupled with an LTS rollforward policy, the controller must ensure hosted API endpoints pinned to an LTS model version do not accidentally get traffic shifted to an incompatible variant. This ticket covers design, implementation, testing, and the first production rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can apply incremental weight changes (min step 0.5%) per region with configurable hold windows
Hold windows are extended automatically when key SLOs (p50 latency, p95 latency, 5xx rate) cross thresholds
LTS-pinned endpoints are excluded from model variant swaps unless a manual rollforward approval is granted
Automated rollback is triggered if error-rate delta or latency delta exceeds configured bounds for contiguous 2-minute windows
Observability: per-route dashboard surfaces weight history, hold reason, and cache-warm factor; alerting integrated with PagerDuty
End-to-end e2e test harness reproduces a lightweight cache-warmup scenario and validates controller behavior in staging
technical_design: Core components: 1) Safeweight Controller service (k8s controller) that interfaces with the orchestration API to mutate regional routing weights, 2) Signal aggregator that subscribes to metric streams (Prometheus / tracing) and emits gating decisions, 3) LTS registry enforcement layer that prevents automated variant swaps for pinned routes, 4) State machine persisted in the controller's CRD to survive restarts. Weight changes are rate-limited by a token-bucket to avoid step spikes; each step includes a preflight canary probe (synthetic request) to measure KV cache hit-rate. Controller exposes a dry-run mode and a protected manual-override path with audit logs.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (staging): deploy controller in a non-production cluster. Run synthetic scenarios that simulate model load and KV miss spike. Duration: 72h
Stage 1 (canary region): enable controller for a single low-traffic region at 1% baseline traffic. Run for 48h and validate metrics and alerts
Stage 2 (regional progressive): after green canary, ramp other regions to 10% increments with 30m default hold windows and adaptive extension on SLO violation
Stage 3 (global): after regional success maintain 24h monitoring and enable LTS rollforward policy for targeted tenants
Backout: automated rollback policy will revert to previous weights and pin controller into reconcile-fail mode if critical metrics breach for >2 mins. Manual on-call runbook attached.
testing_plan: Unit tests for controller state transitions and rate-limiter logic
Integration tests: simulate Prometheus metrics and ensure gating decisions follow expectations
Chaos test: kill controller pod, verify state persisted and reconciliation resumes without spurious weight jumps
Staging e2e: synthetic KV warmup scenario with controlled miss-rate injection and validation of automatic hold/rollback
Load test: run model infer load in staging to evaluate step-wise throughput and latency changes during weight shifts
observability_requirements: Dashboard tile: per-region weight timeline with overlayed p50/p95 latency and 5xx rate
Alert: Weight-change-failed (severity P1) with reason and prior weight snapshot
Audit log: all automatic and manual weight changes persisted to central audit store with actor, reason, and correlation id
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: cascading rollbacks could oscillate across regions -> Mitigation: global cooldown after 3 cross-region rollbacks and circuit-breaker for controller
Risk: KV warmup-related costs increase during slow ramp -> Mitigation: use synthetic pre-warm probes and staggered cache priming
Risk: LTS policy accidentally blocks urgent fixes -> Mitigation: add controlled manual rollforward path with multi-owner approval logged
Risk: insufficient observability -> Mitigation: pair with Observability team to add required dashboards and contract tests

ENG-25401: SLO-aware holdpoint library (provides gating predicates and thresholds)
infra-telemetry: shard-level Prometheus stream with 15s scrape and dedicated metric labels for route/model/version
implementation_notes: Primary language: Go (existing k8s controller patterns). Reuse reconciler scaffolding from ENG-31247.
Config: allow per-customer overrides, default hold windows and thresholds in ConfigMap; secret-backed approval tokens for manual rollforward
Docs: update Runbook (docs/runbooks/hosted-deployments.md) and Console runout UI to show Safeweight state
PRs: expected PRs: controller impl, CRD definitions, observability dashboards, e2e harness changes, runbook updates
